name: Heat Pump Field Commissioning & Connectivity Triage (Telegram)

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: "You are a triage assistant for a heat pump manufacturer's field installers in Germany. An installer has reported a symptom that has no recognized structured fault code, so you must classify it from free text.

Classify the report into exactly one category: hardware_fault, connectivity_issue, or installer_error.
- hardware_fault: the physical unit (compressor, refrigerant circuit, electrical component) is likely broken and needs a technician visit.
- connectivity_issue: the unit itself is likely fine; the HEMS app/pairing/network connection is the problem.
- installer_error: a commissioning step (wiring, pressure fill, sensor orientation, valve position) was likely done incorrectly and can be corrected without escalation.

If manual excerpts are provided below, treat them as authoritative documented guidance and ground your classification and fix_or_escalation_action in them — prefer their specific instructions over generic assumptions. If no excerpts are relevant or none are provided, classify from the symptom text alone as before.

Then provide fix_or_escalation_action: for hardware_fault, an escalation instruction (never step-by-step repair instructions for refrigerant/electrical work — always escalate to a certified technician); for the other two categories, concrete fix guidance the installer can act on immediately.

Respond in the same language the installer used in their message (e.g. reply in German if they wrote in German); reason in English internally but write fix_or_escalation_action in the installer's language.

Respond with ONLY minified JSON, no other text: {"category":"...","fix_or_escalation_action":"...","confidence":0.0}
confidence is your own estimate (0 to 1) of how certain this classification is from the text alone." }, { role: 'user', content: 'Model: ' + $json.model + '\nFirmware: ' + $json.firmware_version + '\nInstaller type: ' + $json.installer_type + '\nFault code: ' + ($json.fault_code || 'none') + '\nReported symptom: ' + $json.reported_symptom + '\n\nManual excerpts (may be none):\n' + ($json.manual_context || 'none') } ] }) }}

assignments.name: message
assignments.value: ={{ 'Escalation required: ' + $json.fix_or_escalation_action + ' — AI-suggested triage, confirm before acting.' + ($json.manual_sources && $json.manual_sources.length ? ' (Grounded in: ' + $json.manual_sources.join('; ') + ')' : '') }}

assignments.name: message
assignments.value: ={{ 'Suggested fix: ' + $json.fix_or_escalation_action + ' — AI-suggested triage, confirm before acting.' + ($json.manual_sources && $json.manual_sources.length ? ' (Grounded in: ' + $json.manual_sources.join('; ') + ')' : '') }}

nodes.name: Log to Monitoring (LangSmith)
nodes.notes: Placeholder for the LangSmith monitoring hook: in production this posts {category, source, confidence, fault_code, model} to a LangSmith run/trace so every triage decision is auditable. See langsmith/ for the Round 1 trace sample and monitoring notes.

parameters.content:
## Step 1 — Classify
Known fault codes (5 synthetic + real Vaillant codes like F.532/F.9998) are resolved by a deterministic lookup — fast, free, fully auditable. Free-text symptoms with no recognized code get a manual-grounded retrieval pass (Retrieve Manual Context), then OpenAI classification. See `data/manuals/` for the sourced manual excerpts and `data/synthetic_fault_dataset.csv` for the original archetypes.

## Step 2 — Route
hardware_fault → escalation to a certified technician.
connectivity_issue / installer_error → immediate fix guidance.
Every response is labeled 'AI-suggested triage — confirm before acting' (human-in-the-loop, EU AI Act limited-risk framing).

## Round 1 POC scope
This is decision support, never an autonomous fix authority — it never issues unsupervised electrical/refrigerant repair steps. Telegram gives free text only, so model/firmware/installer-type default to 'not provided via chat' — see workflow_documentation.md for the production fix. Manual grounding (data/manuals/) uses real Vaillant/Octopus documentation as representative content, not Chleo's own manuals, and keyword (not embedding) retrieval — both stated openly as Round 1 scope. Full safety framing: research/opportunities_risks.md.

## Language handling
The LLM is instructed to reply in whatever language the installer wrote in (German installers get German fix guidance) — modern LLMs handle this natively, no separate translation call needed for the classification step.

The keyword retrieval step is English-only under the hood, so a few German synonyms are mixed into each entry's keyword list as a lightweight bridge. This is partial coverage, not real multilingual search — see workflow_documentation.md -> 'Language' for the fuller recommendation (Round 2: swap to multilingual embeddings, which removes the need for hand-maintained keyword translations entirely).

meta.note: Round 1 capstone POC. Import into n8n, connect a Telegram Bot credential (token from @BotFather) to both Telegram nodes, and set OPENAI_API_KEY as an environment variable before running. See n8n/workflow_documentation.md.
